Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming this land for 40 years, so most of what I do I don't have to think too hard about — I know what works on our 6 mu.

**Our situation**

It's just the two of us at home now. My husband helps some but he also does work off the farm when he can, so the field work mostly falls on me and whatever we can hire for the busy days. Six mu isn't much — we can't afford to waste anything, but we also don't need to treat this like a big operation. Our main goal is to get a decent harvest of wheat and maize, sell some, keep some flour for ourselves, and have a little cash left over.

**Wheat (coming up on harvest now, then replanting in October)**

The wheat going in this October — I'll do what I've done the last few years. I plant around October 8-12, depending on when the maize comes off. I buy seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, the Jimai variety that most people around here use. Maybe 15 kg/mu of seed, costs me around 40 yuan/mu.

For fertilizer, before planting I put down a bag of compound fertilizer (氮磷钾 15-15-15) per mu as base — that's about 40 kg. Then at jointing in spring, if the wheat looks a bit yellow or thin, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg/mu. All told that's around 18 kg N/mu, which the extension man said is about right for our soil. I might do a bit more urea if I see the wheat isn't looking strong.

Irrigation — we have the well, but pumping costs money (electricity and the fee). For wheat I usually do three: winter water before the freeze, jointing water in spring, and grain-filling water in May. If the spring rains come I might skip one. That's my biggest flexible cost.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide in spring once against broadleaf weeds, and I watch for aphids around flowering. If I see them I'll spray, if not I won't.

I hire a combine for harvest — everyone does now, 50-60 yuan/mu, saves my back. I expect around 450 kg/mu if the year is normal. Last year we got close to 470.

**Maize (planting right after wheat harvest in June)**

The turnaround is tight — maize has to go in within a few days of wheat coming off, or I lose growing days in the fall. I buy hybrid seed (Zhengdan or whatever the shop has good stock of that year), about 2 kg/mu, around 50 yuan/mu. I use no-till planting — pay someone with a no-till seeder to come through, it's cheaper than tilling and faster.

For maize I put base fertilizer with the seeder — compound fertilizer again, about 30-35 kg/mu. Then at the big-bell stage (around late July) I topdress urea, maybe 15 kg/mu. So around 15 kg N/mu total, a little less than wheat because maize in summer gets rain.

Irrigation for maize — usually one watering if July-August is dry. Some years I don't irrigate at all. Depends on the rain.

Pesticide — one herbicide spray after planting to handle weeds, and I watch for the maize borer. If it's bad I'll spray once.

Harvest late September, hire the combine again. I expect around 500 kg/mu — maize does pretty well here when rain comes.

**Money**

Total inputs for the year — maybe 700-800 yuan/mu across both crops. On 6 mu that's around 4,500 yuan out. If yields hold up and prices aren't bad, we'll come out with something. Not much, but enough.
